about: The numerics-relevant set of each certification reference lock: the packages whose builds can change what MEEP or the GPU route computes. tools/compare_reference_environment.py judges every name below against the lock files of its platform (conda packages by version and build, PyPI packages by version, origin and, where pypi_build_tags names one, the wheel's build tag) and does not judge the rest of the lock, the compilers and the tools included: the build scripts' step 1b holds the build to every artifact of the lock, and their step 7 to every pin. Package versions live in the lock files; this file adds only what a lock cannot hold: the MEEP the reference builds from source (meep, judged by tools/check_install.py --require-reference, which imports it), the certified environment's own build of a package the lock takes differently by design (by_design), and wheel build tags. Apart from the numerics sets, corpus_only names what the MEEP identity corpus (Table 2) needs and no field update reads: PyPI packages each platform's pip lock pins (shapely, nlopt, imageio-ffmpeg, whose ffmpeg executable the build scripts link into <prefix>/bin), a conda package each conda lock holds (gdspy), and the PyMieScatt stand-in (built from its pinned sdist and patch by the builder it names, which reads its pins from here). The comparison reports them apart and never counts them in its verdict; --require-pip-lock requires the pip lock's packages and the stand-in, exactly.

osx-arm64.basis: MEASURED 2026-10-03: the libraries the certified libmeep and its Python module load (otool closure), the BLAS/LAPACK and OpenMP runtimes NumPy and MEEP reach, the MPI stack, and the Python numerics. libgdsii added 2026-10-14 by the same rule: the reference MEEP is built with libGDSII, and a libmeep of MEEP 1.33.0 built against conda-forge's libgdsii 0.21 links @rpath/libGDSII.0.dylib directly (otool -L, MEASURED 2026-10-14).

hdf5.why: the certified environment holds this nompi build of hdf5; the lock takes the mpi_openmpi build because a nompi HDF5 deadlocks multi-rank MEEP output

linux-64.basis: The Apple silicon set carried over to the Linux packages (libstdcxx for libcxx, libgomp for llvm-openmp, since the Linux MEEP is configured --with-openmp), the UCX/UCC transports of the Linux Open MPI, and the CUDA libraries of the GPU route; checked 2026-10-03 against readelf -d of the round environment's libmeep.so and _meep.so, whose every NEEDED library belongs to a judged package. libgdsii added 2026-10-14 by the same rule: the reference MEEP is built with libGDSII, which configure adds to the libraries libmeep links (AC_CHECK_LIB(GDSII, libGDSIIExists)); the build records the NEEDED list of the images it made (load_commands.json).

corpus_only.about: Needed to re-run the MEEP identity corpus (Table 2), not to compute: a row whose script imports a package, or calls a tool, that the environment lacks is refused by name, never measured. None of them takes part in MEEP's field updates or the GPU route, so none is in a numerics set; importing and calling shapely, nlopt and the stand-in moved no floating-point control flag on either host (MEASURED 2026-10-10). ffmpeg comes from the imageio-ffmpeg wheel, which installs one executable and no shared library; a host's own ffmpeg is not the reference's (the retired host_tools entry).

shapely.why: the PyMieScatt stand-in's Inverse module imports it

imageio-ffmpeg.why: the test is skipped, and the corpus row refused, unless `which ffmpeg` succeeds on the reference PATH (<prefix>/bin:/usr/bin:/bin); the capture stops before ffmpeg is called. The wheel's executable (imageio_ffmpeg/binaries/ffmpeg-*) is linked into <prefix>/bin by the build scripts' step 7b

gdspy.why: the script imports gdspy to write the GDSII file it reads back through MEEP's libGDSII; PyPI has no wheel of gdspy for either platform, so each conda lock holds conda-forge's build

standin.name: PyMieScatt
standin.why: the scripts import PyMieScatt; its 1.8.1.1 release imports trapz from scipy.integrate, which SciPy 1.14 removed, so the stand-in takes it from NumPy
